description: Synthetic decision history for Decision Graveyard Agent demo.

decisions.proposal: Migrate all backend services into a single monorepo to simplify cross-service refactors and unify CI.
reasoning_for: Cross-service refactors currently require coordinating 4 separate PRs
Single CI pipeline would reduce config duplication
reasoning_against: CI p95 build time went from 4m10s to 14m30s
No team was assigned ownership of the monorepo tooling
New hire onboarding time increased because repo size overwhelmed local dev setup
decisions.outcome_evidence: CI p95 build time metrics; all-hands complaint thread with 23 replies before reversal

decisions.proposal: Extract shared UI components into a separate internal package to reduce duplicate frontend code across 3 product teams.
reasoning_for: 3 teams maintaining near-identical button/modal/form components
Design system inconsistency causing UX bugs
reasoning_against: Initial concern about version-locking teams to the same release cadence
decisions.outcome_evidence: Reduced duplicate component code by ~40%; versioning concern addressed with semver + changelog discipline, no major incidents in first 3 months

decisions.proposal: Relaunch outbound cold-calling for enterprise leads to supplement inbound pipeline.
reasoning_for: Inbound pipeline down 18% quarter over quarter
Enterprise deals historically close faster with a live conversation
reasoning_against: Response rate measured at 0.4%, well below the 2% floor set for the pilot
Multiple prospects flagged lead fatigue from repeated contact by other channels
3 formal opt-out complaints filed with legal in the pilot's first month
key_people: Marcus Webb (SDR Lead, ran the pilot)
Ana Torres (VP Sales, called the reversal)
decisions.outcome_evidence: Pilot dashboard: 1,140 dials, 4.6 response rate percent target missed; 3 opt-out complaints

decisions.proposal: Bring back outbound cold-calling, this time targeting only new-market enterprise accounts with no prior contact history.
reasoning_for: Q3 2025 reversal was specifically tied to lead fatigue from over-contacted accounts
New-market accounts have zero prior touchpoints, so fatigue concern does not apply
reasoning_against: Team still lacked a clear playbook for objection handling on cold calls
Response rate improved to 1.8% but still below original 2% target
decisions.outcome_evidence: Trial limited to 400 net-new accounts; response rate 1.8%, approved to continue at reduced scale with quarterly review

decisions.proposal: Shift 40% of paid social budget to short-form video ads on TikTok and Reels.
reasoning_for: Static image ad CTR had declined 30% year over year
Competitor benchmarking showed video-first brands outperforming on CAC
reasoning_against: Concern that video production costs would offset media savings
decisions.outcome_evidence: CAC dropped 22% within two quarters; in-house production kept costs flat after first quarter ramp-up

decisions.proposal: Discontinue the monthly print catalog mailer to cut costs, replacing entirely with email.
reasoning_for: Print mailer cost $180K/quarter with declining measurable attribution
Email open rates for the same segment were healthy
reasoning_against: The 55+ customer segment (18% of revenue) showed a 31% order drop the quarter mailers stopped
Customer service tickets referencing 'I used to get the catalog' rose sharply
key_people: Ron Okafor (CFO, approved reinstatement after revenue dip)
decisions.outcome_evidence: Segment revenue analysis; reinstated at reduced print run (targeted to the 55+ segment only) the following quarter

decisions.proposal: Replace the multi-step checkout flow with a single-page checkout to reduce cart abandonment.
reasoning_for: Cart abandonment rate at 68%, above industry benchmark of ~60%
Competitor analysis showed single-page checkout correlating with lower abandonment
reasoning_against: Concern that combining steps would overwhelm mobile users
decisions.outcome_evidence: Abandonment dropped to 54% within 6 weeks; mobile-specific concern addressed with a collapsible-section mobile layout

decisions.proposal: Add a mandatory account-creation step before checkout to improve customer data capture.
reasoning_for: Only 34% of purchases came from logged-in accounts, limiting personalization and retention marketing
reasoning_against: Cart abandonment spiked from 54% back up to 71% in the first week
Directly undid the single-page checkout win from DEC-007
decisions.outcome_evidence: Abandonment metrics reverted within 72 hours of rollback; guest checkout with optional post-purchase account creation implemented instead

decisions.proposal: Move from a single large nightly deploy to continuous deployment (multiple deploys per day).
reasoning_for: Nightly deploys bundled 15-20 changes, making rollback attribution difficult
Incident post-mortems repeatedly cited 'unclear which change caused this'
reasoning_against: Concern about deploy fatigue and alert noise for on-call engineers
decisions.outcome_evidence: Mean time to identify root cause dropped from 4.2 hours to 40 minutes; on-call alert volume addressed via smarter deploy-window batching

decisions.proposal: Introduce a mandatory 2-hour deploy freeze window around lunch to reduce on-call interruption fatigue.
reasoning_for: On-call engineers reported deploy-related interruptions during lunch as a top complaint in the eng survey
reasoning_against: Freeze window pushed deploys into a backlog that caused a larger batch effect in the afternoon, reintroducing DEC-009's original problem
No measurable change in reported on-call satisfaction after 1 month
key_people: Tomas Reyes (proposed and later withdrew it)
decisions.outcome_evidence: Afternoon deploy batch size increased 3x during the trial; survey scores unchanged; proposal quietly dropped without formal reversal meeting

decisions.proposal: Deploy a fully automated chatbot to handle all tier-1 support tickets with no human fallback option.
reasoning_for: Tier-1 tickets (password resets, order status) made up 62% of volume and were largely repetitive
Support team was over capacity, with average first-response time at 6 hours
reasoning_against: CSAT for bot-only interactions dropped to 2.1/5 vs. 4.3/5 for human-assisted
Customers with edge-case issues had no escalation path and posted publicly on social media
key_people: Ron Okafor (CFO, approved emergency budget for reversal)
decisions.outcome_evidence: CSAT dashboard; 340 social media complaints tagged #NimbusSupport in one week

decisions.proposal: Deploy an AI assistant to triage and draft responses for tier-1 tickets, with mandatory human review before sending.
reasoning_for: Directly addresses the no-escalation-path failure from DEC-011 by keeping a human in the loop
Reduces average handling time without removing human oversight
reasoning_against: Initial concern about reviewer fatigue from reviewing high ticket volume
key_people: Marcus Webb (cross-team input from Sales on tone)
decisions.outcome_evidence: First-response time down to 1.8 hours, CSAT holding at 4.1/5; reviewer fatigue addressed by capping auto-drafts per reviewer per hour

decisions.proposal: Consolidate all analytics tracking onto a single first-party data platform, sunsetting 3 third-party tools.
reasoning_for: 3 overlapping tools cost $210K/year combined with inconsistent metric definitions across teams
reasoning_against: One of the 3 tools (session replay) had no first-party equivalent with feature parity
Full migration timeline of 4 months was cut short at 2 months due to Q3 roadmap pressure
decisions.outcome_evidence: 2 of 3 tools successfully sunset, saving ~$140K/year; session replay tool retained on a reduced contract

decisions.proposal: Switch primary warehouse fulfillment partner to reduce per-order shipping cost.
reasoning_for: New partner quoted 12% lower per-order fulfillment cost
reasoning_against: Average delivery time increased from 2.1 to 4.6 days during peak season
Return rate for damaged items nearly doubled
decisions.outcome_evidence: Delivery time and damage-rate dashboards; reverted to original partner with a renegotiated rate instead

decisions.proposal: Add a second regional fulfillment partner for West Coast orders only, keeping the original partner for all other regions.
reasoning_for: Addresses the original per-order cost concern from DEC-014 without a full cutover
West Coast orders specifically suffered longest transit times under the single-partner model
reasoning_against: Concern about split inventory management complexity
decisions.outcome_evidence: West Coast delivery time down to 1.9 days; inventory split managed via existing WMS with no major incidents

decisions.proposal: Launch a paid loyalty/subscription tier offering free shipping and early access to sales.
reasoning_for: Repeat purchase rate for top-quartile customers was 4x the platform average
Competitor loyalty programs showed strong retention lift
reasoning_against: Concern about cannibalizing existing free-shipping thresholds
key_people: Ron Okafor (CFO, modeled the cannibalization risk)
decisions.outcome_evidence: 18% of eligible customers enrolled in first quarter; free-shipping threshold cannibalization was within modeled range

decisions.proposal: Run a flash 24-hour sitewide 40% discount event to boost quarterly revenue.
decisions.duration_before_reversal: did not repeat after single event
reasoning_for: Q2 revenue was tracking 8% below target with 3 weeks left in the quarter
reasoning_against: Discount attracted heavily price-sensitive one-time buyers with near-zero repeat rate
Margin loss on the event exceeded the revenue gain once returns were factored in
Cannibalized the following week's planned sales, which underperformed
key_people: Jules Ferreira (approved as an emergency measure)
decisions.outcome_evidence: Post-event margin analysis; repeat purchase rate from event buyers measured at 3% vs. 22% baseline

decisions.proposal: Run a flash sale framed as early access for loyalty-tier members only, at a smaller 15% discount.
reasoning_for: Addresses the low-repeat-rate problem from DEC-017 by targeting existing loyal customers instead of the general public
Smaller discount reduces margin risk
reasoning_against: Concern that non-members would feel excluded and complain
decisions.outcome_evidence: Repeat purchase rate from event buyers at 19%, close to baseline; complaint volume from non-members negligible

decisions.proposal: Migrate primary database from PostgreSQL to a distributed NoSQL store to handle scaling concerns.
reasoning_for: Projected 3x order volume growth over the next 18 months
Concerns about write throughput at current scale
reasoning_against: Proof-of-concept migration revealed the actual bottleneck was unindexed queries, not the database engine itself
Estimated migration cost and risk (6+ months, full data layer rewrite) far exceeded the cost of query optimization
decisions.outcome_evidence: Query optimization and read-replica scaling resolved throughput concerns at a fraction of the cost; proposal shelved before full migration began

decisions.proposal: Introduce usage-based pricing as an alternative to flat annual contracts for enterprise clients.
reasoning_for: Several prospects cited flat annual pricing as a blocker during negotiation, preferring to pay for what they use
reasoning_against: Revenue forecasting became significantly harder for the finance team
Only 12% of eligible prospects actually chose the usage-based option once offered
decisions.outcome_evidence: Offered as an optional tier rather than a replacement; forecasting handled via a hybrid model with a usage-based floor

decisions.proposal: Require customers to complete a satisfaction survey before closing any support ticket.
reasoning_for: CSAT response rate was too low to be statistically meaningful (approx. 8% of tickets)
reasoning_against: Mandatory survey created a friction point that delayed ticket closure and inflated handling time metrics
Support agents reported customers becoming frustrated at being blocked from closing their own issue
decisions.outcome_evidence: Handling time metrics spiked 15% in 2 weeks; reverted to optional post-close survey with a follow-up email instead

decisions.proposal: Redesign the mobile app navigation from a tab bar to a hamburger menu to fit more top-level sections.
reasoning_for: Product roadmap wanted to add 3 new top-level sections that did not fit in the existing 5-tab bar
reasoning_against: Engagement with previously one-tap-away sections (Cart, Search) dropped 26% once hidden behind the hamburger menu
User research post-launch showed users perceived the app as harder to use despite no functional loss
key_people: Leo Bramante (UX Research, flagged the engagement drop)
decisions.outcome_evidence: In-app analytics on section engagement pre/post launch; reverted to tab bar with a condensed 5-section structure plus an overflow More tab

decisions.proposal: Build an internal recommendation engine to replace the third-party product recommendation widget.
reasoning_for: Third-party widget cost scaled with traffic and was becoming the single largest vendor line item
Team had accumulated enough first-party interaction data to train a competitive model
reasoning_against: Concern about the multi-month build timeline delaying the cost savings
decisions.outcome_evidence: Click-through rate on recommendations matched the third-party baseline within 5%; vendor cost eliminated entirely after full rollout

decisions.proposal: Adopt a fully serverless architecture for the order-processing pipeline to reduce infrastructure costs.
reasoning_for: Order volume was highly seasonal, and serverless promised to eliminate idle-capacity cost during off-peak periods
reasoning_against: Cold-start latency during Black Friday traffic spikes caused a 90-second processing delay on a subset of orders
Debugging distributed serverless traces proved far harder than the team's existing monitoring tooling supported
decisions.outcome_evidence: Black Friday incident report citing delayed order confirmations; reverted to containerized services with autoscaling instead

decisions.proposal: Move the recommendation engine's inference workload to serverless functions, keeping the core order pipeline containerized.
reasoning_for: Recommendation inference is stateless and bursty in a way order processing (DEC-024) is not, making it a better serverless fit
Avoids repeating the cold-start problem since recommendation latency tolerance is higher than checkout latency tolerance
reasoning_against: Minor concern about a new tooling surface for the team to monitor
key_people: Tomas Reyes (signed off given the DEC-024 lessons)
decisions.outcome_evidence: Inference cost down 34%; no latency complaints in first 2 months

decisions.proposal: Eliminate free returns for orders under $25 to reduce return-processing costs.
reasoning_for: Return processing cost on small orders often exceeded the order's own margin
reasoning_against: Customer complaints on social media and review sites spiked, specifically citing the policy as a reason to shop elsewhere
Conversion rate for orders under $25 dropped 11%, since the free-returns policy was itself a purchase driver
key_people: Jules Ferreira (flagged the review/social sentiment impact)
decisions.outcome_evidence: Review sentiment analysis; conversion rate dashboard for the affected order-value segment

decisions.proposal: Introduce a company-wide standardized event-tracking taxonomy to fix inconsistent metric definitions across teams.
reasoning_for: Marketing, Product, and Data teams were each calculating active user differently, causing conflicting reports in leadership meetings
reasoning_against: Concern about the migration effort required across every team's existing dashboards
decisions.outcome_evidence: All 3 teams migrated within one quarter; leadership reporting discrepancies eliminated

decisions.proposal: Require all enterprise deals over $100K to go through a second-approver sign-off to reduce discounting inconsistency.
reasoning_for: Discount depth on enterprise deals varied wildly rep-to-rep with no consistent rationale
reasoning_against: Added 2-3 days to average deal close time during the pilot, causing at least one deal to be lost to a competitor on timing
Reps reported the approval process as opaque with unclear criteria
decisions.outcome_evidence: Deal-cycle time analysis; threshold raised to $250K and approval criteria published as a scorecard to address the opacity complaint
